[[File:Cavalier Hotel Virginia Beach postcard.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach.]]
[[File:Cavalier Hotel Virginia Beach 2019.jpg|thumb|right|260px|The Cavalier Hotel, 2019. Photo: Carol M. Highsmith.]]
'''1999 Decipher World Championship''' was the fourth Star Wars CCG World Championship, played 12–13 November 1999 at [[DecipherCon 1999]] in the Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia. [[Gary Carman]] (United Kingdom) defeated [[Steven Lewis]] (United States) 2 (+19) and became the first British World Champion.<ref name="trando">[https://web.archive.org/web/20050517110350/http://trandosite.mcmail.com/wf00p2.htm History of the World Finals], [[Trandosite]]</ref><ref name="sw">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128144348/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/index.html Star Wars CCG World Championship], Decipher (Wayback 28 November 1999)</ref><ref name="sat">[https://web.archive.org/web/20001120012500/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/saturday.html Lalumiere Saturday], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 20 November 2000)</ref>

The site was the same Cavalier Hotel that hosted the [[1998 Decipher World Championship]]. [[Kendrick Summers]] announced DecipherCon for the Cavalier Resort and Hotel in Virginia Beach on 27 September 1999.<ref name="rfd26">[https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrkKhWcstAs Broadcast 26 - Radio Free Decipher], Kendrick Summers (27 September 1999). Preserved copy: [https://archive.org/details/youtube-OrkKhWcstAs Internet Archive]. Watch page: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261010122343/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=OrkKhWcstAs Internet Archive].</ref>

The constructed pool was [[Premiere - Endor]]. [[Enhanced Cloud City]] was not legal in the World Championship decks. Decipher sold that product from 9am Saturday for other convention events, including the Invitational and the Sunday Team Challenge.<ref name="ecc">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128112134/http://www.decipher.com/newsflash/1999/1099/102699storyA.html Star Wars CCG Enhanced Cloud City and the '99 World Championships], Kendrick Summers, Decipher (26 October 1999)</ref>

Qualification was more exclusive than 1997–1998: one player per region plus Open, Wild Card, and invitational seats. The regional structure drew heavy criticism and was not kept for 2000. A Wild Card tournament of more than 100 players put [[John Arendt]] and [[James Lafferty]] into the World Finals. Lafferty played all three days. [[Matt Sokol]] placed 3rd in that Wild Card.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="thu">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000903021929/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/lalumiere/thursday.html Lalumiere Thursday], DecipherCon '99 (Wayback 3 September 2000)</ref><ref name="iv16">[http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Matt Sokol interview], [[Trandosite]] (25 October 2000). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20041026224145/http://www.trandosite.mcmail.com/iv16.htm Internet Archive]</ref> [[Joe Alread]] won Ironman and missed the main event for the first time.<ref name="trando" />

Day 1 (32 players, eight games): [[Bastian Winkelhaus]] led on 13 (143), then [[Clint Hays]] on 13 (80). Carman finished third on 12 (71) after a strong close. [[Matt Lush]] finished 28th. That evening Carman lost his decks and rebuilt overnight, borrowing and adjusting Markus Wuest's Light.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="final12">[https://web.archive.org/web/20000122170128/http://decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/final12.html They advanced to the Round of 12], Decipher (Wayback 22 January 2000)</ref><ref name="lush">Matt Lush, [https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/1999-11-16-day-one-world-championshipsd110/ day-one-world-championships], DeckTech (16 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20261009094534/https://www.stephenskilton.com/decktech_archives/reports/1999-11-16-day-one-world-championshipsd110/ Internet Archive]</ref>

Day 2 (four games): [[Yannick Lapointe]] was the early leader; Winkelhaus and Hays took early losses. Lewis was the only undefeated and met Carman (Naboo region) in the final.

Final game 1: Carman [[ISB Operations / Empire's Sinister Agents|ISB Operations]] (Outer Rim Scout) against Lewis's Clak'dor VII Operative Speeder ([[Local Uprising / Liberation|Local Uprising]]). Carman won by 22. Game 2: Carman [[Hidden Base / Systems Will Slip Through Your Fingers|Hidden Base]] inserts against Lewis [[Hunt Down And Destroy The Jedi / Their Fire Has Gone Out Of The Universe|Hunt Down]]. Lewis probed the Hidden Base with Security Precautions. Carman resolved Never Tell Me The Odds for 8 after Grimtaash stripped Torture. Lewis won by 3 with Lateral Damage. Combined, Carman 2 (+19).<ref name="trando" /><ref name="tfn">[http://www.theforce.net/videogames/story/CCG_World_Champion_78174.asp CCG World Champion], TheForce.Net (14 November 1999). Preserved copy: [https://web.archive.org/web/20160101143010/http://www.theforce.net/videogames/story/CCG_World_Champion_78174.asp Internet Archive]</ref> [[Mark Tuttle]] called game 2 the most exciting match he had ever watched, and Decipher posted his play-by-play audio of both games.<ref name="trando" /><ref name="sw" /> Francis K. Lalumiere called Carman's win the last World Champion title of the millennium.<ref name="sat" />

== Format ==

* '''Environment:''' [[Premiere - Endor]] ([[Enhanced Cloud City]] excluded)<ref name="ecc" />
* '''Site:''' [[DecipherCon 1999]], Cavalier Hotel, Virginia Beach, Virginia
* '''Dates:''' Worlds Day 1 Friday 12 November 1999; Day 2 and Final Confrontation Saturday 13 November. The convention ran 11–14 November.
* '''Field:''' 32 (4 Open + 2 Invitational + 23 Regional + 2 Wild Card + 1 defending). Thursday Wild Card: 146 Star Wars players; [[John Arendt]] and [[James Lafferty]] took the two seats.<ref name="field">[https://web.archive.org/web/19991128125001/http://www.decipher.com/calendars/event/mainevents/deciphercon/swworldchamp/finalists.html Finalists], Decipher (Wayback 28 November 1999)</ref><ref name="thu" />

== Qualifiers ==

Decipher listed 32 finalists for the World Championship.<ref name="field" /> The field was 4 Open, 2 Invitational, 23 Regional, 2 Wild Card, and the defending champion [[Matt Potter]].<ref name="field" />

Thursday 11 November 1999 was the Wild Card. Francis K. Lalumiere wrote at 9:10 p.m. that 146 Star Wars players were still in that event, and that the World Championship started on Friday.<ref name="thu" /> [[John Arendt]] and [[James Lafferty]] took the two seats.<ref name="field" /><ref name="trando" /> [[Matt Sokol]] placed 3rd; only the top 2 advanced to the World Finals.<ref name="iv16" />
